sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by impermeable fluorescent-substrate staining (CA-Alexa488 for HaloTag, BG-Alexa488 for SNAP-tag) in COS-7 cells; correct molecular weight shift confirmed by Western blot. No explicit ligand-binding or signalling functional assay result is reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: ACVR2B is a single-pass Type II receptor with its sole extracellular terminus at the mature N-terminus (residue 19 onward after SP cleavage at 18/19). The paper explicitly places the tag 'downstream of the signal peptide sequence', which by the authoritative topology landmarks (SP = 1–18) maps unambiguously to insert_after_residue = 18, i.e. between G18 (last SP residue) and S19 (first mature residue). Python verification confirms seq[17]='G' and seq[18]='S'. The junction is 119 residues from the TM boundary (138), well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint. Because the paper names the landmark but not a residue number, position_evidence is topology_derived; there is exactly one extracellular terminus so no ambiguity remains. PMC9837045 generated a full-length BMP/TGFβ receptor library in which hACVR2B was cloned into pcDNA3.1 with an N-terminal Halo- or SNAP-tag placed downstream of the signal peptide sequence and separated from the receptor by a 5× glycine linker. The construct was expressed in COS-7 cells. Western blot confirmed molecular weights consistent with successful tagging (L3), and impermeable CA-Alexa488 / BG-Alexa488 staining confirmed surface display of the tagged receptor (L4).

sources.claim: Further, all Halo- and SNAP-tagged receptors were positively detected using impermeable CA-Alexa488 or BG-Alexa488 staining, respectively.

literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) derive from the same publication (PMC9837045) and describe the same construct and experiment. L1 and L2 establish the construct design (N-terminal Halo/SNAP after SP, 5× Gly linker, full-length receptor in pcDNA3.1, COS-7 expression). L3 confirms correct MW by Western blot. L4 provides the strongest evidence: surface display confirmed by impermeable dye staining. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion or a C-terminal extracellular tag (the C-terminus is intracellular). No ledger line reports a tolerated intracellular insertion or a function-abrogating insertion, so other_positions is empty.
